A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InftyThink+ research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections, including v1 Appendix B with v3 Appendix K.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results, including accuracy, token usage, latency, ablations, and repeated-run stability analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds the efficiency-reward decay experiments in Appendix P.

M1.justification: The proposed cold-start procedure, iterative rollout, quadratic efficiency reward, trajectory-level GRPO optimization, and IcePop stabilization remain unchanged. Linear and logarithmic rewards are introduced as ablation alternatives, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain OpenThoughts-114K and DeepScaleR-Preview training data and the same mathematical, scientific, and code evaluation coverage. The new decay ablation reuses MATH500, AIME24, and AIME25.

E2.justification: Appendix P newly evaluates linear- and logarithmic-decay variants against the quadratic reward variant. These add ablation comparators; existing comparisons with vanilla RL, SFT-only models, alternative summarization strategies, and DeleThink remain.

E3.justification: The new decay experiment introduces reward shape as a controlled training condition, tracking checkpoint accuracy and reward/iteration dynamics through 1,000 steps. Existing experiments retain their reported model sizes, training budgets, decoding settings, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix P adds a focused sensitivity analysis of efficiency-reward decay. Figures 28-30 compare penalty strength, downstream accuracy, task reward, efficiency reward, and iteration count. The extensive earlier ablations and stability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over 32 sampled completions and the same three-run training and evaluation stability studies, moved from Appendix K to J. The new decay experiments introduce no stated additional replication or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 29-30 add results showing late-training collapse with linear decay and degradation with logarithmic decay, while quadratic decay maintains stronger final accuracy. Existing table results remain unchanged, including 50.94% task-only AIME24 accuracy in Table 1; the DeleThink comparison curves are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix P adds mathematical definitions of linear and logarithmic efficiency rewards and states their ordering relative to quadratic decay for 0 < x < 1. The original information-bottleneck and computational-complexity arguments move from Appendix B to K without substantive changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about trajectory-level RL, adaptive iterative reasoning, accuracy gains, generalization, and computational efficiency. The new ablation supports an existing design choice without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix P adds the interpretation that aggressive efficiency penalties encourage premature termination, motivating quadratic decay as a softer regularizer. The new Impact Statement also qualifies environmental benefits through potentially increased usage. Existing methodological limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 identifies H200 GPUs for data preparation, training, and evaluation; v3 removes the GPU model and retains generic GPU descriptions. This reduces hardware documentation without establishing an actual hardware change. The detailed hyperparameter tables remain.

R1.justification: The Ling Team 2025c reference changes from 'Every Step Evolves: Scaling Reinforcement Learning for Trillion-Scale Thinking Model' to 'Every Attention Matters: An Efficient Hybrid Architecture for Long-Context Reasoning,' with different listed coauthors. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata, while research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v3 removes the contents pages, relocates the theoretical appendix, trims some redundant explanations, and adds conflict-of-interest, acknowledgements, and impact sections. These are limited structural and editorial revisions.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a conference-style document with a two-column main text, substantially changed typography, headers, and figure placement. Several plots are resized, Figure 2's caption expands, and Figures 28-30 are added. Figure 20 also introduces erroneous 'w/o RL' labels for RL-trained variants.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix P provides useful empirical support for the quadratic reward choice and identifies a premature-termination failure mode, modestly strengthening the paper. This gain is tempered by removed H200 hardware details and incorrect Figure 20 labels. The central method and previously reported results remain stable.
